pr.title: Anonymous: Add configurable device limit

raw_findings.body: TypeScript infers the class property type as literal `undefined`, so numeric comparisons/uses of the value are type errors and the value can never be legally assigned a number through the typed class, defeating the purpose of the new setting.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Type checking narrows the property to `undefined`, breaking numeric consumers of the config value.
raw_findings.impact: TypeScript infers the class property type as literal `undefined`, so numeric comparisons/uses of the value are type errors and the value can never be legally assigned a number through the typed class, defeating the purpose of the new setting.
raw_findings.root_cause: The added field omits a type annotation, so TS infers `undefined` instead of the `number | undefined` declared in the GrafanaConfig interface.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit annotation matching the interface: `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined;`.
raw_findings.title: anonymousDeviceLimit field is typed as `undefined` only, not `number | undefined`
raw_findings.trigger: Any frontend code that reads `config.anonymousDeviceLimit` through the `GrafanaBootConfig` class type and uses it numerically (e.g. `config.anonymousDeviceLimit > 0`) after bootData merge populates it with a number.

raw_findings.body: Every anonymous authentication now blocks on the device count/insert/update DB round-trip that was previously performed in a detached goroutine with its own timeout, adding synchronous latency and DB load to the auth hot path even when no device limit is configured.
raw_findings.evidence: if err := a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, httpReqCopy, anonymous.AnonDeviceUI); err != nil {
raw_findings.failure_mode: Auth latency and database pressure increase for the common no-limit configuration.
raw_findings.impact: Every anonymous authentication now blocks on the device count/insert/update DB round-trip that was previously performed in a detached goroutine with its own timeout, adding synchronous latency and DB load to the auth hot path even when no device limit is configured.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch removed the background goroutine and timeout context and now calls TagDevice inline in Authenticate for all cases.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Only perform tagging synchronously when a device limit is configured (cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit > 0); otherwise retain the non-blocking background tagging path.
raw_findings.title: Anonymous device tagging changed from async to synchronous on every request
raw_findings.trigger: Any anonymous request authenticating through the Anonymous client, including deployments where `device_limit` is 0 (the default).

raw_findings.body: The newly introduced `device_limit` key is undiscoverable through the standard configuration reference, contrary to Grafana's convention of documenting every ini setting.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Documentation drifts from the implemented settings surface.
raw_findings.impact: The newly introduced `device_limit` key is undiscoverable through the standard configuration reference, contrary to Grafana's convention of documenting every ini setting.
raw_findings.root_cause: A new ini key was added without the corresponding documentation/default entries required by convention.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a commented `device_limit` entry under `[auth.anonymous]` in conf/defaults.ini and conf/sample.ini and document it in the configuration reference.
raw_findings.title: New `device_limit` setting not documented in defaults/sample ini
raw_findings.trigger: An operator looking up available `[auth.anonymous]` options in conf/defaults.ini, conf/sample.ini, or the configuration docs.

finding.verifier_reason: The class implements GrafanaConfig interface which declares `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined` (line 200 in config.ts). TypeScript class property initializers without explicit type annotations infer from the interface when implementing it. The `update` method merges bootData settings, overwriting the undefined default. The claim that TS infers literal `undefined` preventing numeric assignment is incorrect - the interface type governs the property type.

finding.verifier_reason: Patch removes goroutine+timeout wrapper (lines L45-L57) and calls TagDevice synchronously inline (R44). The TagDevice implementation performs DB operations (CountDevices, CreateOrUpdateDevice). When device_limit=0 (default), the count check is skipped but upsert still runs synchronously on every anonymous auth request, adding latency to the auth path that was previously non-blocking.
